subject: QBR prep: KPI triage, tune recommendations, and action owners
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-09-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: QBR prep: KPI triage, tune recommendations, and action owners

Team — attaching the September KPI pack (sheet + raw samples) ahead of next week’s QBR prep slot. High-level flags I want on the radar before we finalize slides: 

- Latency: p95 stable but p99 tail shows two ~120ms spikes on 9/10 and 9/12 that align with a config change to fallback routing. Need root cause and short mitigation.
- Cost: month-over-month token spend up ~14% driven by an increase in smaller models being used as fallbacks for heavy chat traffic; per-token cost savings on batching look promising but we need safety checks.
- Uptime: a 0.5% availability dip during a maintenance window impacted some dedicated customers; we should confirm SLO attribution and postmortem owner.
- Usage: OptiScale (external) shows a shift to more short, high-concurrency queries between 00:00–06:00 UTC — could change batching profile.

Asks: 
1) Irene — can you own the uptime postmortem and a 1-slide summary with RCA + mitigation by EOD Tuesday (2027-09-21)? Include impact window and affected capacity pools.
2) Vivek — run a per-route cost delta for September vs August and a short sensitivity analysis for increasing batch sizes (simulate 5%, 10%, 20% throughput gain) by Thursday COB (2027-09-23).
3) Marissa — synthesize a single leadership slide that captures the metric trends + 3 recommended actions (one for latency, cost, uptime) by Friday morning so I can fold into the QBR deck.

I’ve flagged a few sample traces in latency-samples.json (attached) and the KPI workbook has a 'slide-ready' tab. If OptiScale can share a small sample of concurrent traffic (CSV) that would help Vivek's sim.

Thanks — Neha
Neha Kapoor
Head of Platform Ops | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: 2027-09-monthly-kpis.xlsx, latency-samples.json

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-09-18T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QBR prep: KPI triage, tune recommendations, and action owners

Thanks — I’ll take the postmortem. Quick notes from a first pass on the spike: the two 120ms p99 events line up with the rollout of a new fallback policy that added a model-variant hop when pool A exceeded 65% utilization. My plan:

- Collect the rollout logs + routing decisions for 9/10–9/13
- Validate whether KV cache warming was impacted by the fallback loop
- Produce an RCA + short-term mitigation (rollback or hard threshold) and a long-term control (better rollout guardrails)

Irene (I’ll need the exact list of affected customer pools from infra; Neha, can you ping infra ops if needed). Also propose we invite the OptiScale contact to the Friday sync for usage context.

On owners: agree with Vivek owning cost sim; I’ll sync with him after he has OptiScale samples.

— Irene
Irene Choi
SVP, Platform | Redwood Inference

From: Kyle Brown <kyle@optiscale.io>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-09-19T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QBR prep: KPI triage, tune recommendations, and action owners

Neha / Irene — thanks for the heads up. We dug into our telemetry and can share a 7-day sample of concurrent requests and a histogram of request lengths (attached). Quick context: over the last month our client SDK updated to batch more aggressively for throughput-heavy workflows, but a small subset of customers reverted which increased short, chat-like traffic between midnight and 06:00 UTC. That aligns with your short, high-concurrency pattern.

Attached: optiscale-concurrency-20270910-16.csv (7-day sample) and a small CSV with per-customer daytime vs nighttime ratios. We’re fine joining the Friday sync; my ask: can Redwood run a small experiment that increases host-level batching from 4->6 for a 6-hour window and report latency p99 and error rates? We’re happy to provide traffic routing to a test pool.

— Kyle
Kyle Brown
Prod Ops Lead | OptiScale
kyle@optiscale.io

Attachments: optiscale-concurrency-20270910-16.csv, optiscale-daynight-ratio.csv

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kyle Brown <kyle@optiscale.io>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-09-19T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QBR prep: KPI triage, tune recommendations, and action owners

Kyle — appreciate the sample; that’s exactly what Vivek will need. We can run the 6-hour host-level batching test in a canary pool; Vivek, please coordinate with OptiScale for traffic routing.

Proposed quick steps and owners (we’ll confirm in the Friday slot):
- Experiment: Host batching 4->6, 6-hour canary (Vivek) — target window: Tue 9/21 01:00–07:00 UTC. Metric capture: p50/p95/p99, error-rate, CPU/GPU utilization.
- Uptime PM: postmortem slide + recommended fix (Irene) — deliver draft by Tue EOD (2027-09-21).
- Cost sim: per-route delta + sim results (Vivek) — deliver preliminary numbers Wed COB (2027-09-22).
- Leadership slide: condensed summary + recommended asks (Marissa) — deliver by Fri 9/24 morning.

Meeting: I’ll schedule a 30-min sync on Friday (9/24) to finalize the QBR page. If we can confirm data from the experiment by Wed AM, I’ll mark that as a call-out on the slide.

On the experiment thresholds: our initial goal is to demonstrate >=10% cost-per-op improvement in the canary without p99 increasing by more than 10ms and with no increase in failed requests. If that baseline looks good, we can recommend a phased rollout.

Thanks all — I’ll drop a calendar invite and link to the drive.

— Neha
Neha Kapoor
Head of Platform Ops | Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-09-21T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: RE: QBR prep: KPI triage, tune recommendations, and action owners — sync notes and action list

Folks — recap after the short sync with OptiScale and infra: 

Decisions: 
- Run the host batching canary Tue 9/21 01:00–07:00 UTC (traffic routed by OptiScale). Vivek to execute test and push telemetry to the shared folder.
- If canary meets thresholds (>=10% cost/op improvement, p99 delta <= 10ms, no spike in errors) proceed to a staggered rollout across non-dedicated pools.

Action items (owner — due):
- Vivek Kulkarni — run the 6-hour canary, capture p50/p95/p99, error-rate, CPU/GPU metrics, and upload raw telemetry + a 1-page summary to Drive (due 2027-09-22T14:00:00-07:00).
- Irene Choi — finalize uptime postmortem slide with RCA and short-term mitigation (due 2027-09-21T23:59:00-07:00).
- Marissa Cole — produce leadership-ready slide with trend bullets and the recommended go/no-go criteria for rollout (due 2027-09-24T09:00:00-07:00).
- Neha Kapoor — prepare the QBR page and note the canary outcome; draft contingency language for customers if rollout is paused (due 2027-09-24T12:00:00-07:00).

Artifacts shared: Drive link (https://drive.google.com/open?id=1q2w3eQBR-kpi-boards), KPI workbook, OptiScale sample CSV in folder, latency-samples.json.

If any owner needs more time, flag ASAP — we need the canary outcome before finalizing the QBR recommendation.

— Neha
Neha Kapoor
Head of Platform Ops | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com
